title: Marimba
summary: The marimba is the national instrument of Guatemala: wooden bars graduated in length, each over its own resonator, struck with rubber-headed mallets. Players roll fast repeated strokes to hold a note and play melody, harmony and bass on one keyboard.
howToPlay: Ten wooden bars lie in order of pitch, shortest and highest at the top.
Notes are named C to E' in the usual European way.
Strike each bar as its note lands, and treat quick repeated notes as a roll that holds the note.
Start with the son in six, then try the rolled melody and the bass and tune.
rules: The bars follow a European major scale: seven notes to the octave, so ten bars reach the third note of the next octave.
The son is counted in six pulses, grouped in twos and threes.
A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
heritageNote: The first record of a marimba in Guatemala dates from 1680, an instrument with gourd resonators; later makers built larger keyboards and, in 1894, a double keyboard. Marimba bands remain a part of village and town life.
